representativeRepos.readmeText:
Auto Ontology

 Agents can retrieve documents and query databases, but reliability gates agentic analytics: a revenue metric answered faster is worth nothing if the number is wrong. Agents need a context layer that tells them where data lives, what it means, whether to use it, how to use it, where it came from, and what is similar. NVIDIA Auto Ontology is an open library that builds that layer from enterprise metadata, reconciles definitions across systems, and exposes it to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API. It complements the semantic models customers already own.

 It enables developers to:

- Discover: generate enterprise ontologies from metadata; connect existing ontologies and semantic models; build AI-ready knowledge graphs.

- Ground: give agents trusted business meaning for metrics, entities, and relationships; reconcile inconsistent definitions across systems.

- Validate: check generated queries against certified definitions and lineage; return provenance with every answer.

- Expose: serve context to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API.
Learn: fold certified corrections and usage back into the ontology, so shared context improves with every question.

 Benchmarks

 To run a text-to-SQL benchmark such as BIRD, refer to the
 ontology SQL evaluation repository .

 Licensing & contributions. Auto Ontology is distributed under the
 Apache License 2.0 . Third-party open-source components
bundled, linked, or otherwise used by this project are listed in
 THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md . This project
is currently not accepting external contributions.

 Key Features

- Natural-language querying of structured data — questions are translated to
SQL and executed against connected databases, powered by NVIDIA NIM.

- Semantic catalog / ontology layer over relational sources, stored in
Postgres alongside the catalog it describes.

- Authentication & RBAC —using Better Auth .

- Web UI for chat, analysis, data catalog, analytics, and settings.

- Flexible deployment — Helm chart for Kubernetes or Docker Compose for a
local stack.

 Software Components

 Component
 Technology
 Role
 Default port

 Frontend
 Next.js 16 (React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4), Better Auth, Prisma
 Web UI, authentication, API gateway
 3000

 Backend
 FastAPI (Python 3.12+), LangChain
 Chat / NL-to-SQL, catalog, datasource APIs
 3001

 Ingestion worker
 FastAPI (Python 3.12+)
 Ingests tabular data and writes embeddings
 3002

 Postgres + pgvector
 Relational Database
 App metadata, the catalog and ontology, vector store
 5432

 HashiCorp Vault
 Optional
 Secure storage of connection credentials
 —

 NVIDIA NIM

 Auto Ontology uses NVIDIA NIM endpoints for inference — either the hosted
 NVIDIA API catalog ( integrate.api.nvidia.com ) or
self-hosted NIMs. The defaults in .env.example are:

- LLM: nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b

- Embeddings: nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b

- Reranking: nvidia/llama-nemotron-rerank-vl-1b-v2

 The endpoints and models are configured via the DEFAULT_MODELS_ENDPOINT , DEFAULT_MODELS_MODEL ,
 EMBED_ENDPOINT , and EMBED_MODEL environment variables and require a
 DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY .

 Model triplets

 Each model role is configured by a triplet of environment variables —
 <PREFIX>_ENDPOINT (URL), <PREFIX>_API_KEY , and <PREFIX>_MODEL :

 Prefix
 Role

 DEFAULT_MODELS
 Shared default; every field below falls back to it.

 REASONING
 Main chat / NL-to-SQL model.

 NON_REASONING
 Lighter model used for entity extraction.

 EMBED
 Text-embedding model (must match between ingest and query).

 RERANK
 Reranker used by the retrieval flow.

 You can set a full triplet, only some of its fields, or none at all — any field
left unset falls back to the matching DEFAULT_MODELS_<FIELD> . So the simplest
setup is to fill in DEFAULT_MODELS_* and override per-triplet fields only where
they differ (e.g. EMBED_MODEL , NON_REASONING_MODEL ). *_API_KEY also falls
back to the legacy NVIDIA_API_KEY for backward compatibility.

 Quickstart

 This runs Auto-Ontology with Docker Compose against Wide World Importers,
Microsoft's sample sales database. You need Docker with Compose v2,
 uv , and an NVIDIA API key ( nvapi-... ) from
 build.nvidia.com .

-
 Clone the repository and create .env :

 git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology.git && cd auto-ontology
cp .env.example .env

 Then set these values in .env :

 DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY = nvapi-...
 AUTH_SECRET = <a long random string, e.g. from openssl rand -base64 32>
 APP_URL = http://localhost:3000
 POSTGRES_PASSWORD = <a new password>
 CONNECTION_STRINGS = postgresql://postgres:<the same password>@postgres:5432/wideworldimporters
 AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_PASSWORD = <a new password>
 PGADMIN_PASSWORD = <a new password>

 Compose publishes Postgres, pgAdmin, and the web app on the host, so replace
each default password before you start it. .env.example also sets an API
key per model role: replace each nvapi-your-api-key-here with your key, or
delete those lines so they fall back to DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY .

-
 Start Postgres and load the sample database. The seed script lives in
auto-ontology-eval; pass it the Postgres password you set:

 docker compose up -d --wait postgres
git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology-eval.git ../auto-ontology-eval
(cd ../auto-ontology-eval && uv sync && cp .env.example .env && \
 POSTGRES_PASSWORD= ' <the same password> ' \
 uv run python scripts/seed/seed_wwi.py --database-name wideworldimporters --drop)

-
 Build and start the rest of the stack:

 docker compose up -d --build

-
 Open http://localhost:3000 and sign in with AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_EMAIL and
 AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_PASSWORD from .env . Go to Settings → Semantic
Compilation and turn it on. Ingestion runs at startup; compilation starts
immediately and reports Semantic compilation is ready when it finishes.

-
 Ask a question in Chat :

 What was revenue for the USB food flash drive - sushi roll in Pennsylvania
in June 2015?

 The agent resolves revenue , product , and state to terms in the
ontology, follows their relationships to the joins it needs, and runs the
query. The answer comes back with its SQL and the steps that produced it,
so you can check the result against the source:

 Answer: Revenue for USB food flash drive - sushi roll in Pennsylvania in
 June 2015 was $588.80, from 3 invoice lines.

SQL: SELECT SUM(il.extendedprice) AS revenue, COUNT(*) AS invoice_lines
 FROM sales.invoicelines il
 JOIN sales.invoices i ON il.invoiceid = i.invoiceid
 JOIN warehouse.stockitems si ON il.stockitemid = si.stockitemid
 JOIN sales.customers c ON i.customerid = c.customerid
 JOIN application.cities ct ON c.deliverycityid = ct.cityid
 JOIN application.stateprovinces sp ON ct.stateprovinceid = sp.stateprovinceid
 WHERE si.stockitemname = 'USB food flash drive - sushi roll'
 AND sp.stateprovincename = 'Pennsylvania'
 AND i.invoicedate >= '2015-06-01' AND i.invoicedate < '2015-07-01'

Steps: Resolved terms: Invoice Line (revenue), Stock Item, State Province, Invoice
 Joined: invoice line -> invoice -> customer -> city -> state province
 Validated the filter values against the data, then executed

-
 Ask something the data can't answer. Wide World Importers has no
advertising data, so a question about ad spend has nothing to resolve
against. An agent connected through MCP checks answerability
first and asks you to clarify:

 You: What was return on ad spend for the sushi roll flash drive in June 2015?
Agent: check_answerable -> coverage 0.5; no term covers "ad spend"
Agent: I can find revenue for that product, but this data has no
 advertising spend, so I can't compute return on ad spend. Do you
 want June 2015 revenue instead, or is ad spend tracked in another
 source I should connect?

 If the UI loads without its left navigation after a restart, the browser is
holding a stale session cookie. Clear site data for localhost:3000 and sign in
again. For other setup failures, see the
 setup skill's troubleshooting guide .

 How it works

 Auto-Ontology works in three stages: it generates an ontology, people certify
it, and the agent answers questions from it.

 The ontology holds three kinds of definition:

- Terms. Business concepts such as Customer or Invoice Line , each with a
description and synonyms, mapped to the columns that hold them.

- SQL attributes. Reviewed SQL expressions under a term, such as a margin or
a rolling total. The agent reuses them, so answers compute each measure the
same way.

- Relationships. How tables join, including bridge tables, inferred from
keys and from the data.

 Generate. The ingestion service builds a first draft from the source
databases:

- Read sources: extract schemas, profile columns, and sample values into the
catalog.

- Name entities: extract terms table by table and map each to columns.

- Resolve relationships: infer joins between tables and bridge tables, and
suggest SQL attributes from query history.

- Write the ontology: store terms, relationships, and SQL attributes in
Postgres, with embeddings in pgvector for retrieval.

 The result is a semantic graph you can explore in the UI. In this example, one
compilation of Wide World Importers produced 31 terms; selecting Order shows
its description, related terms, mapped columns, and SQL attributes:

 Certify. People make the draft trustworthy:

- Test with real questions in Chat, or with check_answerable and
 ask_question over MCP.

- Refine terms, descriptions, and SQL attributes in the UI or through the API.

- Certify names, descriptions, and SQL attributes once they're correct.

 Answer. For each question, the agent:

- Classifies the intent and extracts the entities the question names.

- Retrieves candidate terms, columns, and SQL attributes by embedding search.

- Writes SQL from those candidates.

- Checks the filter values and the query against the database, repairing the
SQL when a check fails.

- Runs the query and returns the answer with its SQL and the steps it took.

 When the candidates can't support a query, the agent reports that the question
can't be answered from this data. Predictive questions go to KumoRFM when it's
configured (see Predictions ).

 In Chat, each answer shows its SQL, and you can view the rows, download them as
CSV, or read them as a chart:

 Auto-Ontology is compatible with Apache Ossie , the
open standard for exchanging semantic models. Ossie includes a
 converter for Auto-Ontology ,
which Auto-Ontology uses to import and export model definitions as Ossie YAML.
Use Settings → Import / Export , or POST /api/model/import and
 POST /api/model/export .

简体中文 | 繁體中文 | English | 日本語 | Türkçe | Español | Čeština

 全能的光盘盘面可见图像生成与刻录工具

 Disc Image Studio 是一个多平台的光盘盘面图像生成与刻录工具，帮助您使用任何刻录光驱在任何 DVD / CD / 单层蓝光 光盘上刻蚀出肉眼可见的图像。

 效果预览

 概述

 Disc Image Studio 可将一张图片转换成符合 CD、DVD 与单层 BD-R 光盘物理层约束的数据，刻录后将使光盘盘面呈现肉眼可见的图案。

 界面预览

 快速开始

 Windows 下载 win-x64.exe 后可直接运行。Linux 或 macOS 请下载与 CPU 匹配的 实验性 CLI 压缩包，解压后运行 ./disc-image-studio --help 。这些发布包均自带 .NET 运行时。 GitHub Releases

 1. 新建工程

 在主页选择 CD、DVD 或蓝光，指定输出位置后创建工程。

 2. 设计盘面

 在设计页导入图片，用图层完成排版，并在右栏「影调」模块调整抖动、伽马、亮度与灰阶档位。

 3. 预览与导出

 在预览页核对盘面投影，在导出页生成 ISO / RAW / WAV+CUE，或使用即时刻录功能直接写入空白盘片。

 即时刻录为实验性功能，请只使用可报废的测试介质。

 功能

 光盘数据生成

- CD 支持 ：支持任何 CD 。您可导出带格式头的 WAV 音轨及配套 CUE，兼容 cdrecord, ImgBurn等刻录软件；也允许导出 RAW 音轨。详见 CD 刻录兼容说明 。

- DVD 支持 ：支持任何 DVD。您可导出 ISO 镜像。

- 蓝光支持 ：支持任何单层 BD-R 25 GB，支持纯绘图与 UDF 2.01 文件。详见 ADDING_BLURAY.md 。

- 随盘文件 ：CD／DVD／蓝光可在设计页直接选择要保存的文件夹及内圈／外圈位置，也可在导出页调整；设置随工程保存。

- 文件区域预览 ：混合盘的设计投影和成品读回用黄色标出文件区（含文件系统）。

- 介质灰度方案 ：CD 与 DVD 均使用黑白二阶，CD 使用 0D / AA ，DVD 扰码域使用 A5 / 92 。详见 PHYSICAL_MODEL_AUDIT.md 。

- 灰度抖动工具 ：独立程序也可将原图处理为 0/255 黑白二阶 PNG；支持打开或拖入原图、并排预览及无损 PNG 导出。详见 使用与构建说明 。

- 盘片预设 ：内置数个品牌的光盘参数，覆盖 CD／DVD／BD。您也可将自己标定好的数据贡献给我们，详见 预设维护说明 。

 辅助标定

 Disc Image Studio 提供粗标定、边界标定和精细标定流程，通过盘面照片估计内外半径与轨距分布。下面的历史实盘对比中，校准前采用恒定轨距，十字线的径向线条出现明显弯曲；使用辅助标定得到的三次轨距参数重新生成并刻录后，线条更接近径向直线。实测精度取决于照片矫正、取点和复刻验证，参数保存的小数位数不代表测量精度。

 校准前 · 恒定轨距
 校准后 · 三次轨距

 P20261004-133519.jpg
 P20261004-135416.jpg

 第一次使用可跟随 DVD 标定实操教程：Verbatim AZO DVD-R ，查看照片矫正、三个标定阶段的实际取点、参数变化与参考值，以及精标后的盘面效果。完整流程与参数说明见 辅助标定说明 。

 刻录

- 镜像文件输出 ：您可以导出完整 ISO / RAW 文件并使用合适的刻录软件手动刻录。

- 即时流式刻录（实验性） ：CD、DVD 与 BD-R 边生成边刻录，不保存完整镜像；BD-R 走 MMC 顺序写入。

- 不要使用非空白介质！

 系统与设备要求

- 桌面版需要 Windows 10 2004（2004/20H1，19041）及以上，或 Windows 11。

- 构建：.NET 10 SDK（ global.json 锁定 10.0.x）；自行构建的非自包含 GUI 需要 .NET 10 Windows 桌面运行时。Release EXE 已包含运行时，无需另行安装 .NET。

- “即时刻录”功能需要一台 Windows 可识别的 CD / DVD / BD 刻录机与空白盘片；BD-R 需要支持顺序写入的单层空白盘。

 构建与运行

 dotnet build DiscImageStudio.slnx -- configuration Release
dotnet run -- project src / DiscImageStudio.App -- configuration Release

 构建回归检查：

 dotnet run -- project src / DvdImageSolver -- configuration Release -- selftest
dotnet run -- project tests / DiscImageStudio.ArchitectureTests -- configuration Release

 版本规则、CI 生成 EXE、Release 草稿检查、MSIX 打包与签名流程见 发布指南 。

 命令行

 Linux（glibc）可选 linux-x64 或 linux-arm64 。Apple Silicon Mac 选 osx-arm64 ，Intel Mac 选 osx-x64 。CLI 在本地生成镜像，实际写盘可交给支持相应镜像或音轨的刻录软件。

 使用 .NET 10 SDK 从源码运行 CLI

 dotnet run --project src/DiscImageStudio.Cli -c Release -- --help

 CLI 可读取 PNG、JPEG、BMP 和 GIF，使用动画图片的第一帧。下面的例子用两扇区音轨验证安装，同时生成配套 CUE。

 ./disc-image-studio cd-generate --input picture.png --output sample.wav --sectors 2

 命令
 说明

 solve
 使用固定快速纹理映射（CW 方向）生成 DVD 镜像，黑白纹理可选抖动混合

 encode
 将单个 DVD ECC 块编码为 NRZI 通道电平

 calibrate
 标定投影：按生成几何从 DVD 源图片取样，按实测几何投到盘面

 simulate
 按实测半径对生成的 DVD ISO 做读回模拟

 selftest
 运行 DVD 引擎的确定性回归自检

 cd-generate
 无随盘文件时生成 WAV + CUE / RAW 音轨；指定 --data-dir 时生成 CD 数据盘 ISO

 cd-preview-warp
 标定投影：按实测几何投影 CD 源图片

 cd-preview-track
 按标定几何渲染已有的 WAV 或 RAW CD-DA 音轨（读回模拟）

 bd-generate
 生成完整 BD-R ISO，并写出 <iso>.json sidecar

 bd-info / bd-probe / bd-encode
 导出 BD 参数、原始负载探针或单个 ECC 簇诊断

 各命令的完整参数见对应文档。

 源码结构

 src/DiscImageStudio.Cli/ Linux 和 macOS 离线命令行入口
src/DiscImageStudio.ImageIO/ WIC 和跨平台图像编解码
src/DiscImageStudio.Core/ 介质无关的模块契约、工程/预设模型、任务与命令目录
src/DiscImageStudio.Imaging/ CD/DVD/BD 共用的图片预处理与抖动辅助
src/DiscImageStudio.Burning/ Windows IMAPI2 设备枚举、流缓冲与安全刻录层
src/DiscImageStudio.Cd/ CD-DA 生成核心与 CD 模块
src/DiscImageStudio.Dvd/ DVD 引擎适配模块
src/DiscImageStudio.BluRay/ BD-R 几何、17PP/ECC、3T/6T 映射、流式生成与 ISO
src/DiscImageStudio.Iso/ UDF 2.01 / ISO9660 写入器
src/DiscImageStudio.App/ WPF GUI、统一命令行与商店资源
src/DvdImageSolver/ 保持隔离的 DVD 编码/求解引擎
tests/ 无第三方测试框架的架构回归测试
packaging/ MSIX 清单与打包脚本
tools/ 独立辅助工具与资产生成脚本
docs/ 架构、引擎、预设、发布等文档

 文档

 文档
 内容

 ARCHITECTURE.md
 模块抽象、层间边界与扩展规则

 LOCALIZATION.md
 界面语言配置、系统语言回退与翻译资源维护

 DVD NRZI 图像约束求解器的约定、编码链与自检覆盖

 CD_AUDIO_COMPATIBILITY.md
 CD 音轨格式、字节序与重影排查

 ADDING_BLURAY.md
 蓝光模块的物理模型、生成/刻录链路与扩展点

 DISC_PRESETS.md
 可编辑盘片预设的分层 JSON 格式与合并规则

 CALIBRATION.md
 照片矫正、三阶段取点示例、三次轨距拟合与再次精标

 CALIBRATION_TUTORIAL.md
 Verbatim AZO DVD-R 实操教程：三个阶段的真实记录、取点图与精标后效果

 PHYSICAL_MODEL_AUDIT.md
 CD / DVD 生成物理模型复核

 VALIDATION.md
 各轮构建、回归与实盘测试的本地验证记录

 RELEASING.md
 GitHub Release、MSIX 打包、签名测试与商店提交流程

 CHANGELOG.md
 版本变更记录

 参考标准

 Disc Image Studio 的实现与物理模型主要参考以下规范：

 介质
 标准与版本
 本项目采用的范围

 CD-R
 ECMA-394，第 1 版，2010 年 12 月 — Recordable Compact Disc Systems CD-R Multi-Speed （ 官方 PDF ）
 CD-R 介质、多速录制及 CD-DA 兼容关系；本项目生成 CD-DA 音轨。

 DVD 公共格式 / DVD-ROM
 ECMA-267，第 3 版，2001 年 4 月 — 120 mm DVD – Read-only disk （ 官方 PDF ）
 DVD 数据帧、ECC、EFMPlus 编码及附录 G 转换表；可记录盘的介质规则另参考 ECMA-359。

 DVD-R
 ECMA-359，第 1 版，2004 年 12 月 — 80 mm (1,46 Gbytes per side) and 120 mm (4,70 Gbytes per side) DVD Recordable Disk (DVD-R) （ 官方 PDF ）
 单层 DVD-R 的几何、扇区、纠错和编码；标准包含单面及双面介质，双面不等于双层。

 BD-R
 ISO/IEC 30190:2021，第 3 版，2021 年 1 月 — 120 mm 单层（25.0 GB）及双层（50.0 GB）可记录 BD 的信息交换与存储规范
 实验模式采用单层 25 GB 的轨道、扇区布局、纠错和编码；目前不支持双层盘。

 CD 公共编码部分还参考了 ECMA-130，第 2 版（CD-ROM，1996） 。

 刻录与介质安全须知

- Disc Image Studio 不安装驱动或服务；“即时刻录”功能使用了 Windows 自带的 IMAPI2，拒绝非空白介质。

- “即时刻录”功能已有部分实盘反馈，对不同设备、介质与刻录入口的验证覆盖仍有限，属于实验性功能，请只使用可报废的测试介质。刻录中断、断电或生成速度不足仍可能使盘片报废！

- 实际可见效果取决于盘片、刻录机、固件与写入策略。

- 混合文件夹会在开始刻录前扫描目录并固定布局；期间源文件大小改变会安全终止任务，已开始写入的盘片仍可能报废。

- BD-R 顺序写入不提供备用区重映射；中断后同一盘片通常不能继续写入。

 隐私与安全

- Disc Image Studio 不联网、不上传文件、不收集遥测，详见 隐私政策 。

- 发现安全问题请不要在公开 Issue 中披露，按 安全政策 使用 GitHub 私密报告。

 贡献

 欢迎报告问题与提交代码。开发环境搭建、模块边界规则、测试要求与 Pull Request 流程见 贡献指南 。

 许可证

 项目采用 GNU GPL v3.0 or later （ GPL-3.0-or-later ）。CD 交织实现包含从 CDImage 移植并修改的代码，整体分发沿用兼容的 GPL 授权；分发二进制或修改版时须遵守对应源代码等要求。第三方字体与组件遵循各自许可证，详见 授权说明 和 第三方声明 ；应用"关于"页也可离线查看完整文本。

 致谢

 感谢 arduinocelentano 的 CDImage 项目 ，它展示了通过生成 CD 音轨在盘面形成可见图像的方法。本项目的 CD 交织实现由其相关代码移植并继续修改，CD 盘面绘图思路也受其启发。CDImage 原作者及贡献者的工作为本项目提供了重要基础。

representativeRepos.readmeText:
Scenario Agent Skills

 Agent Skills that teach AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, and 70+ others) how
to create production-ready content with Scenario through the
 Scenario MCP server : images, video, audio, textures, skyboxes, 3D
assets, and custom-trained models, for games, entertainment, and any creative vertical.

 The expert tools at the bottom of the list work differently: teams of skills that drive DCC (digital
content creation) software and game engines installed on your machine (ZBrush, Blender, Maya, Unreal
Engine, Unity, Godot, Roblox Studio), distilled from expert tutorials, conference talks, and
official documentation. They need the application, not the Scenario MCP server, and each family
folder's README records how it was built and how far it was verified.

 Skills follow the Agent Skills format.

 Install

 Everything for Scenario. Every Scenario skill, without the expert tools: the default for working
through the Scenario MCP.

 # Every Scenario skill, without the expert tools
npx skills add scenario-labs/skills --skill scenario scenario-inspiration scenario-image scenario-multi-reference scenario-product-shots scenario-brand-kit scenario-image-editing scenario-text-overlay scenario-storyboards scenario-game-assets scenario-sprite-animation scenario-side-view-game-kit scenario-blender-2d-animation scenario-textures scenario-skyboxes scenario-3d scenario-video-to-motion scenario-blender scenario-patina-retexture scenario-orbit-views scenario-walkable-room scenario-video scenario-video-editing scenario-video-color-grade scenario-seedance-music-video scenario-kinetic-music-video scenario-chatgpt-pet-create scenario-chatgpt-pet-update scenario-seedance-storyboard scenario-seedance-drafts scenario-video-ads scenario-ugc scenario-fan-cam scenario-reel-recast scenario-audio scenario-video-assembly scenario-motion-loops scenario-caption-studio scenario-consistency scenario-identity-library scenario-model-training scenario-asset-analysis scenario-quality-gate scenario-refine-loop scenario-model-comparison scenario-formats scenario-workflows scenario-workflow-authoring scenario-moderation scenario-report scenario-team-admin scenario-admin-analytics scenario-gpt-image scenario-mai-image scenario-seedream scenario-gemini-image scenario-reve scenario-ideogram scenario-grok-imagine-image scenario-luma-image scenario-minimax-video scenario-gemini-omni scenario-grok-imagine-video scenario-veo scenario-seedance scenario-kling scenario-vidu scenario-wan scenario-runway scenario-luma-video scenario-minimax-music scenario-elevenlabs scenario-ace-step scenario-sonilo scenario-meshy scenario-rodin scenario-sparc3d scenario-3d-worlds scenario-ad-variants scenario-thumbnails

 By role or goal. INSTALL.md groups the skills by job, from 2D artist to producer,
and by outcome, from game art to ChatGPT pets, with one command each.

 Expert tools. A family installs as one set, since its specialists import the lead skill's
scripts: select its "Expert tools" group in the installer menu, or run the command in its family
README ( ZBrush , Blender ,
 Maya , Unreal Engine ,
 Unity , Godot ,
 Roblox Studio ).

 Pick, or install one skill.

 # Pick from the installer menu, grouped by topic (it opens with nothing preselected: select before pressing enter)
npx skills add scenario-labs/skills

 # A single skill
npx skills add scenario-labs/skills --skill scenario

 Pin a reviewed release. The commands above fetch the latest copy of each skill from main . To
install a reviewed state instead, pin both the installer and the commit, taken from a release's tag.
Run it again with a newer commit to move.

 npx skills@1.7.4 add scenario-labs/skills# < commit > --skill < name >

 The menu's topic groups cannot be selected from the command line: the CLI matches --skill against
exact skill names only, and a group flag is an open request upstream
( vercel-labs/skills#992 ). From a script or CI,
run the default command above or a role command from INSTALL.md with -y , which skips every prompt.

 The Scenario skills need the Scenario MCP server connected:

 claude mcp add --transport http scenario https://mcp.scenario.com/mcp

 Or add https://mcp.scenario.com/mcp to any MCP client and sign in with a Scenario account (OAuth),
or use an API key . Full setup lives in the scenario
skill.

 Staying up to date

 Releases are how changes become visible: every feature, fix, and documentation change merged to
 main lands in the next release, staged by release-please as an open release PR. Merging that PR
tags a version, updates CHANGELOG.md in this repository, publishes a
 GitHub release , and posts the notes to the
 Scenario changelog .

- To learn that a skill changed, watch this repository's releases (Watch, then Custom, then Releases
on GitHub) or check any of the changelog pages above. An entry scoped to a single skill carries
that skill's name; changes spanning several skills appear under broader scopes such as skills .

- To pull the changes, run npx skills update where you installed, or re-run your original
 npx skills add command.

- To stay on a reviewed state, pin the install (see Install ).

 Skills

 Getting started

 Connect the Scenario MCP server and learn the core generation loop every other skill builds on.

 Skill
 Use it for

 scenario
 Connecting to the Scenario MCP and the core generation loop: discover, schema, run, wait, display, download

 Finding a direction

 Turn a blank brief into references, options someone can choose between, and a moodboard the next
batch runs from.

 Skill
 Use it for

 scenario-inspiration
 Finding a direction before generating: serendipity, reference hunting, A/B/C/D concept options, moodboard collections

 Images

 Generate and edit images: model choice, sizing, references, masked edits, post-processing tools, and
letter-perfect text overlay cards.

 Skill
 Use it for

 scenario-image
 Text-to-image and image editing: model choice, sizing fields, prompt limits, reference images, masked inpainting

 scenario-multi-reference
 One image composed from several references, each with one job (subject, place, pose, style, palette), leaks checked

 scenario-product-shots
 Product photography from a real photo: packshots, lifestyle scenes, relighting, label-fidelity gates

 scenario-brand-kit
 Visual identities: SVG logos and wordmarks, palette and type specs, gated variants and applications, the filed kit

 scenario-image-editing
 Tool-model image edits: 3D LUT grades, effects, expand and reframe, resize, slicing, layers, background removal

 scenario-text-overlay
 Letter-perfect text overlays: templated transparent PNG cards (taglines, CTAs, legal supers, rich cards) to composite

 scenario-storyboards
 Comic pages, storybooks, and pre-viz storyboards: script first, one run per panel, a locked cast, lettering in post

 scenario-thumbnails
 Finished video covers with character fidelity, exact copy and small-preview readability

 Game art and 3D

 Sprites, icons, tilesets, textures, skyboxes, 3D models, and walkable spaces for games, the web, and
interactive scenes.

 Skill
 Use it for

 scenario-game-assets
 Sprites, icons, props, tilesets, pixel art, concept art, transparent backgrounds, style-consistent batches

 scenario-sprite-animation
 Walk cycles, idle loops, VFX sprites, and animation sheets from one prompt: GIF vs sprite sheet output, frame slicing, pixel cleanup

 scenario-side-view-game-kit
 Side-scroller and platformer art: side-view pixel sprite strips for a hero and enemies (run, walk, attack, hurt, poses), parallax layers, seamless wall texture, platform strip, props

 scenario-blender-2d-animation
 A side-scroller shot animated in Blender from Scenario pictures: a concept frame that locks the look, parallax layers, props and a hero run cycle on its reference, flat image cards with an orthographic camera, keyed jumps and rigid-body props, and a whole new look by swapping the pictures

 scenario-textures
 Seamless and tileable textures, PBR materials, tiling-safe upscaling, engine-ready sizing

 scenario-skyboxes
 360 equirectangular panoramas and skyboxes, seam-safe upscaling, engine export

 scenario-3d
 Text or image to 3D meshes, multi-view reconstruction, retexture and remesh, inline 3D preview, GLB/FBX download

 scenario-video-to-motion
 Motion capture from a reference or generated video: an uploaded character auto-rigged and animated, or motion alone on a Mixamo or MetaHuman skeleton, with in-place, looping, and engine-ready exports

 scenario-blender
 Drive an open Blender scene through the Scenario for Blender extension's local MCP server: read the scene, quote and run generations, capture viewport references, place results, plan camera paths

 scenario-patina-retexture
 PATINA PBR retexture of a finished mesh: material families, one map set per family, Blender apply with geometry untouched, matched before/after comparison film

 scenario-orbit-views
 New camera angles of one picture through a 3D intermediary: clay layouts in a grounded panorama, repaint per camera, matched transparent set

 scenario-walkable-room
 A room from one interior photo to walk into: clean plate, splat world, PBR props with impact sounds, splat-based calibration, physics viewer with grab and throw

 Video and audio

 Video generation, editing, and color grading, seamless motion loops, music, sound effects, voice,
and speech.

 Skill
 Use it for

 scenario-video
 Text-to-video and image-to-video, motion prompting, lipsync, video editing, upscaling, cut/split/concat utilities

 scenario-video-editing
 Tool-model footage edits: LUT grades and effects, trim, split, resize, reverse, frames, masks, layers

 scenario-video-color-grade
 Code-written grades on existing footage: looks, relight, log to Rec.709, reference match, one kept color with masks, .cube LUTs, a showreel

 scenario-seedance-music-video
 Turning a song into a music video: beat-aligned shots, lyric transcription, shot sound under the master, assembly

 scenario-seedance-storyboard
 Movement that holds across cuts: timecoded shot scripts, character sheets and boards, pose-chained shots that play as one performance

 scenario-seedance-drafts
 Cheap 480p Seedance takes reviewed and ranked, only the picks finalized to 1080p, with the draft-versus-final cost math

 scenario-video-ads
 Producing a video ad from a product shot: brief, storyboard, cinematic grammar, fidelity gates, budget, delivery

 scenario-ad-variants
 Ordered independent campaign edits from existing footage, preserving original gameplay and audio

 scenario-audio
 Music, sound effects, voice and speech generation, video scoring, audio utilities

 scenario-video-assembly
 Assembling clips into a finished video: timeline composition, concat with transitions, overlays, music, captions

 scenario-motion-loops
 Seamless brand-color motion loops in code (backgrounds, bumpers, shape animations) rendered to MP4, with a Scenario cut-out over them

 scenario-caption-studio
 Captioning a finished video per destination: styled burn-in or SRT, transcription hints, translation, per-platform placement

 Socials

 Made for social feeds and chat apps: UGC-style creator videos, fan-cam reactions from a photo, trend
reels recast with your own character, kinetic-typography lyric videos, and animated ChatGPT and
Codex pets, new or updated.

 Skill
 Use it for

 scenario-ugc
 UGC-style creator video: talking-head and avatar ads, demos, faceless voiceover, spoken-register scripts, claim safety

 scenario-fan-cam
 Personalized fan-cam clips: identity edit into a broadcast still, reaction beats to video, graphics composited in post

 scenario-reel-recast
 A trending reel performed again by your character: same moves, camera and song, outfit swaps, a redecorated room

 scenario-kinetic-music-video
 Kinetic-typography music video, landscape or 9:16: style frames and footage from Scenario, a JavaScript engine for lyric type on sung onsets, mattes, per-sec...

 Persistent memory compression system built for Claude Code .

 Quick Start •
 How It Works •
 Search Tools •
 Documentation •
 Configuration •
 Troubleshooting •
 License

 Claude-Mem seamlessly preserves context across sessions by automatically capturing tool usage observations, generating semantic summaries, and making them available to future sessions. This enables Claude to maintain continuity of knowledge about projects even after sessions end or reconnect.

 Quick Start

 Install claude-mem for Grok Bot:

 npx claude-mem install --ide grok-bot

 Grok Bot has no host hooks, so we watch the chat log files. Default is CMEM Pro, the hosted memory. Local observer is opt-in: --provider host . Installing this plugin does not install Cursor.

 Awareness push pilot (LFG + Orifice): needle observations ( decision , bugfix , security_alert , sensitive ) are appended as dated - YYYY-MM-DD [awareness] … lines into that bot's memory/log/YYYY-MM.md . Grok Bot already re-reads the log from disk. This does not write profile.md , user-memory, or project memory. Disable with CLAUDE_MEM_GROK_BOT_AWARENESS_ENABLED=false .

 Install with a single command:

 npx claude-mem install

 The installer sets everything up first, then asks you to sign in to claude-mem in your browser (email magic link — no card required). Signing in provisions a memory key for your account and unlocks the claude-mem observer with a 30 Day Free Trial : memory runs off-plan, so you get up to 100% more usage from your plan. When the free trial ends, memory automatically falls back to your Anthropic plan unless you subscribe. After sign-in you pick your memory provider — the claude-mem observer, your own OpenRouter or Gemini key, or your Anthropic plan.

 Prefer to skip the sign-in? Pass an explicit --provider flag, set CLAUDE_MEM_ONLINE_OPTIN=false , or run in CI/non-interactive shells — the installer completes without any account interaction.

 Or install for OpenCode:

 npx claude-mem install --ide opencode

 This works with OpenCode 1.3.4 or later, including OpenCode 2. Restart OpenCode after installing.

 Or install for T3 Code (Codex and Claude Code providers):

 npx claude-mem install --ide t3code

 The installer discovers T3 Code's enabled providers, registers native Claude-Mem plugins in their configured homes, and supports T3-managed Codex. Restart T3 Code, trust the provider's hooks when prompted, and start a new thread. See the T3 Code integration guide for custom server settings, status, and removal.

 Or install for Antigravity CLI ( setup guide ):

 npx claude-mem install --ide antigravity

 Or install for OMP (Oh My Pi):

 npx claude-mem install --ide omp

 Or install the native Pi extension or DeepSeek Harness plugin:

 npx claude-mem install --ide pi
npx claude-mem install --ide dsh --dsh-profile tui

 Pi and DeepSeek Harness use the worker runtime. See native harness setup for capture, recall, and troubleshooting.

 Or install from the plugin marketplace inside Claude Code:

 /plugin marketplace add thedotmack/claude-mem

/plugin install claude-mem

 Restart Claude Code. Context from previous sessions will automatically appear in new sessions.

 Note: Claude-Mem is also published on npm, but npm install -g claude-mem installs the SDK/library only — it does not register the plugin hooks or set up the worker service. Always install via npx claude-mem install or the /plugin commands above.

 🦞 OpenClaw Gateway

 Install claude-mem as a persistent memory plugin on OpenClaw gateways with a single command:

 curl -fsSL https://install.cmem.ai/openclaw.sh | bash

 The installer handles dependencies, plugin setup, AI provider configuration, worker startup, and optional real-time observation feeds to Telegram, Discord, Slack, and more. See the OpenClaw Integration Guide for details.

 Key Features:

- 🧠 Persistent Memory - Context survives across sessions

- 📊 Progressive Disclosure - Layered memory retrieval with token cost visibility

- 🔍 Smart Search (Default) - Query your project history with the three-step mem-search skill

- 🖥️ Local My Work - Live requests, progress, human handoffs and a saved review queue at the worker URL printed on startup. Guide . Memory, sessions and settings remain at /viewer .

- 👥 TeamBrain - An optional shared workspace beside My Work, with real team work lists, member attribution and linked findings. Each person chooses what to share; personal requests and review notes stay separate. Set up a team .

- 💻 Claude Desktop Skill - Search memory from Claude Desktop conversations

- 🔒 Privacy Control - Use <private> tags to exclude sensitive content from storage

- 🖼️ Screenshots (opt-in, off by default) - Keep converted copies of tool screenshots under ~/.claude-mem/media-v1/ , upload them to cmem.ai only when Cloud Sync is on, and send them to the observer model only when image inference is separately enabled ( details )

- ⚙️ Context Configuration - Fine-grained control over what context gets injected

- 🤖 Automatic Operation - No manual intervention required

- 🔗 Citations - Reference past observations with IDs through the worker API or view all in the web viewer

 Documentation

 📚 View Full Documentation - Browse on official website

 Getting Started

- Installation Guide - Quick start & advanced installation

- Usage Guide - How Claude-Mem works automatically

- Search Tools - Query your project history with natural language

- Cloud Sync - Back up your memories to cmem.ai — no daemon, the worker syncs on write

 Best Practices

- Context Engineering - AI agent context optimization principles

- Progressive Disclosure - Philosophy behind Claude-Mem's context priming strategy

 Architecture

- Overview - System components & data flow

- Architecture Evolution - The journey from v3 to v5

- Hooks Architecture - How Claude-Mem uses lifecycle hooks

- Hooks Reference - Every hook entry explained

- Worker Service - HTTP API & Bun management

- Database - SQLite schema & FTS5 search

- Search Architecture - Hybrid search with Chroma vector database

 Configuration & Development

- Configuration - Environment variables & settings

- Development - Building, testing, contributing

- Troubleshooting - Common issues & solutions

 How It Works

 Core Components:

- Lifecycle Hooks - SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd. Each is one shell-free command, claude-mem hook claude-code <event> , run by a small launcher that the installer puts on PATH

- Smart Install - Cached dependency checker (Setup hook on claude --init / --maintenance , plus npx claude-mem install / repair )

- Worker Service - Local HTTP API with web viewer UI and search endpoints, managed by Bun

- SQLite Database - Stores sessions, observations, summaries

- mem-search Skill - Natural language queries with progressive disclosure

- Chroma Vector Database - Hybrid semantic + keyword search for intelligent context retrieval

 See Architecture Overview for details.

 MCP Search Tools

 Claude-Mem provides intelligent memory search through 4 MCP tools following a token-efficient 3-layer workflow pattern :

 The 3-Layer Workflow:

- search - Get compact index with IDs (~50-100 tokens/result)

- timeline - Get chronological context around interesting results

- get_observations - Fetch full details ONLY for filtered IDs (~500-1,000 tokens/result)

 How It Works:

- Claude uses MCP tools to search your memory

- Start with search to get an index of results

- Use timeline to see what was happening around specific observations

- Use get_observations to fetch full details for relevant IDs

- ~10x token savings by filtering before fetching details

 Available MCP Tools:

- search - Search memory index with full-text queries, filters by type/date/project

- timeline - Get chronological context around a specific observation or query

- get_observations - Fetch full observation details by IDs (always batch multiple IDs)

 Example Usage:

 // Step 1: Search for index
 search ( query = "authentication bug" , type = "bugfix" , limit = 10 )

 // Step 2: Review index, identify relevant IDs (e.g., #123, #456)

 // Step 3: Fetch full details
 get_observations ( ids = [ 123 , 456 ] )

 See Search Tools Guide for detailed examples.

 System Requirements

- Node.js : 20.0.0 or higher

- Claude Code : Latest version with plugin support

- Bun : JavaScript runtime and process manager (auto-installed if missing)

- uv : Python package manager for vector search (auto-installed if missing)

- SQLite 3 : For persistent storage (bundled)

 Windows Setup Notes

 If you see an error like:

 npm : The term ' npm ' is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet

 Make sure Node.js and npm are installed and added to your PATH. Download the latest Node.js installer from https://nodejs.org and restart your terminal after installation.

 Claude Code hooks do not need Git Bash. Each hook runs claude-mem directly, and npx claude-mem install places that launcher at %LOCALAPPDATA%\claude-mem\bin\claude-mem.exe and adds the folder to your user Path. Restart your terminal or IDE afterwards so Claude Code picks up the new Path. If hooks report Executable not found in $PATH: "claude-mem" , run npx claude-mem doctor and see Troubleshooting .

 Configuration

 Settings are managed in ~/.claude-mem/settings.json (auto-created with defaults on first run). Configure AI model, worker port, data directory, log level, and context injection settings.

 To include observations from every harness in Claude Code and Codex SessionStart context, set "CLAUDE_MEM_SESSION_START_INCLUDE_ALL_SOURCES": "true" in that file, or enable Include all sources at session start in the viewer settings. The default is "false" , which limits startup context to the current harness. The observation count limit still applies across the selected sources.

 See the Configuration Guide for all available settings and examples.

 Mode & Language Configuration

 Claude-Mem supports multiple workflow modes and languages via the CLAUDE_MEM_MODE setting.

 This option controls both:

- The workflow behavior (e.g. code, chill, investigation)

- The language used in generated observations

 How to Configure

 Edit your settings file at ~/.claude-mem/settings.json :

 {
 "CLAUDE_MEM_MODE" : " code--zh "
}

 Modes are defined in plugin/modes/ . To see all available modes locally:

 ls ~ /.claude/plugins/marketplaces/thedotmack/plugin/modes/

 Available Modes

 Mode
 Description

 code
 Default English mode

 code--chill
 Records fewer observations, keeping only what would be painful to rediscover

 code--[lang]
 Same as code , with observations and summaries written in another language

 Built-in language codes: ar , bn , cs , da , de , el , es , fi , fr , he , hi , hu , id , it , ja , ko , nl , no , pl , pt-br , ro , ru , sv , th , tr , uk , ur , vi , zh . For example, code--ko writes memories in Korean.

 See Modes for each language's name, the email investigation mode, and custom modes.

 Note: All of these modes are built in. No additional installation or plugin update is required.

 After Changing Mode

 Restart Claude Code to apply the new mode configuration.

 See the Development Guide for build instructions, testing, and contribution workflow.

 If experiencing issues, describe the problem to Claude and the troubleshoot skill will automatically diagnose and provide fixes.

representativeRepos.readmeText:
agent-desktop

 Computer use for AI agents: see and operate desktop apps on macOS, Windows, and Linux through the OS accessibility tree.

 agent-desktop gives an AI agent computer use without screenshots or pixel matching. It reads the accessibility tree of a desktop app and returns it as JSON, with a ref for every element the agent can act on. The agent clicks or types on a ref, reads the UI again to check the result, and repeats. The loop lives in your agent; agent-desktop has no model inside. It ships as a CLI and a C library.

 Snapshots, clipboard reads, screenshots, command output, and debug artifacts can contain private desktop content. Keep them out of public logs and uploads.

 Install

 npm install -g agent-desktop
agent-desktop status # platform, permissions, supported surfaces
agent-desktop permissions --guide # macOS: walks you through the Accessibility grant

 Bun, Yarn and pnpm can install the same package. It includes native binaries and platform helpers for x64 and ARM64.
For direct execution without a JavaScript launcher, download the matching native archive from
 GitHub Releases and keep its helper beside the executable.

 On macOS and Linux, Homebrew also works: brew install agent-desktop . There is no official Scoop package yet.
The repository no longer maintains a custom Homebrew tap or Scoop bucket.

 Release archives and building from source are covered in Installation .

 Quick start

 agent-desktop snapshot --app Finder -i # interactive elements, each with a ref
agent-desktop click @s8f3k2p9:e8 # act on a ref from that snapshot
agent-desktop snapshot --app Finder -i # observe again to verify

 Each command prints one JSON envelope. A trimmed snapshot:

 {
 "version" : " 2.6 " ,
 "ok" : true ,
 "command" : " snapshot " ,
 "data" : {
 "app" : " Finder " ,
 "snapshot_id" : " s8f3k2p9 " ,
 "ref_count" : 59 ,
 "complete" : true ,
 "tree" : {
 "role" : " window " ,
 "name" : " Downloads " ,
 "children" : [
 { "role" : " treeitem " , "name" : " Documents " , "ref_id" : " @s8f3k2p9:e8 " , "available_actions" : [ " Click " ] }
 ]
 }
 }
}

- Refs carry their snapshot id. A bare @e8 fails with INVALID_ARGS .

- If the UI changed, an action returns STALE_REF or AMBIGUOUS_TARGET . Take a new snapshot and use its refs.

- Actions are headless by default: no pointer movement, no focus change. Pass --headed for physical input.

- type , set-value , and clipboard-set accept --stdin for piped text, keeping it out of process arguments. Run secret steps as separate commands; batch JSON text appears in process arguments.

- In PowerShell, quote every ref ( '@s8f3k2p9:e8' ), because a bare @token is the splatting operator.

 The full walkthrough is in the quick start .

 How it works

 Your agent calls the CLI, or the C library in process. Both run the same core, which reaches the OS only through PlatformAdapter . Each binary is built for one OS and talks to that OS's accessibility API.

 For AI agents

 The binary carries guides that match its version:

 agent-desktop skills get desktop # the loop, refs, verification and retry rules
agent-desktop skills get platform # what differs on the OS you run on
agent-desktop < command > --help # flags for one command

 Install the skill into an agent harness from skills.sh :

 npx skills add https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop --skill agent-desktop

 Or add this to your AGENTS.md :

 Use ` agent-desktop ` to see and operate desktop apps. Before the first use, run
 ` agent-desktop skills get desktop ` and ` agent-desktop skills get platform ` , and follow them.

 Retry a failed command only when error.disposition.retry is safe . See JSON output for the envelope, error codes, and exit codes.

 MCP

 agent-desktop mcp serves every command as an MCP tool over stdio. A tool is named after its command ( desktop_snapshot , desktop_click , desktop_session_start ), takes that command's arguments, and returns its JSON envelope:

 { "mcpServers" : { "agent-desktop" : { "command" : " agent-desktop " , "args" : [ " mcp " ] } } }

 Global flags given to mcp , such as --session , --headed or --trace , apply to every call.

 Commands

 agent-desktop has 60 command names, 56 operational commands. The other four ( key-down , key-up , mouse-down , mouse-up ) refuse to run until a daemon can release a held key or button. Commands documents each one.

 Group
 Commands

 Observe
 snapshot , find , get , is , screenshot , list-surfaces

 Act on a ref
 click , double-click , triple-click , right-click , type , set-value , clear , focus , select , toggle , check , uncheck , expand , collapse , scroll , scroll-to

 Keyboard and mouse
 press , hover , drag , mouse-move , mouse-click , mouse-wheel , key-down , key-up , mouse-down , mouse-up

 Apps and windows
 launch , close-app , list-apps , list-windows , list-displays , focus-window , resize-window , move-window , minimize , maximize , restore , open-system-surface

 Notifications
 list-notifications , dismiss-notification , dismiss-all-notifications , notification-action

 Clipboard
 clipboard-get , clipboard-set , clipboard-clear

 Wait
 wait

 Sessions
 session , trace , cursor-overlay

 System
 status , permissions , version , batch , skills

 Platform support

 Platform
 Requirement
 Accessibility API

 macOS
 macOS 13 or later, Intel or Apple Silicon
 AX API

 Windows
 Windows 10 1809 or later, x64 or ARM64
 UI Automation

 Linux
 Ubuntu 24.04 or later, x86_64 or aarch64, X11 or Wayland
 AT-SPI

 Each platform page lists what works headless, what needs --headed , and what refuses.

 C library

 Each release ships libagent_desktop_ffi , so a program can call agent-desktop in process. See the C library docs .

 import ctypes
 lib = ctypes . CDLL ( "./lib/libagent_desktop_ffi.dylib" )
 lib . ad_adapter_create . restype = ctypes . c_void_p
 lib . ad_adapter_destroy . argtypes = [ ctypes . c_void_p ]
 assert lib . ad_init ( 7 ) == 0 # AD_RESULT_OK when the header's AD_ABI_VERSION_MAJOR matches the library
 adapter = lib . ad_adapter_create ()
 lib . ad_adapter_destroy ( adapter )

 Development

 Each platform adapter builds only on its own OS, so scope cargo to the host's packages. On macOS:

 HOST_PKGS=(-p agent-desktop-core -p agent-desktop-macos -p agent-desktop -p agent-desktop-ffi)
cargo test " ${HOST_PKGS[@]} "
cargo clippy " ${HOST_PKGS[@]} " --all-targets -- -D warnings

 On Windows, use agent-desktop-windows instead of agent-desktop-macos ; on Linux, agent-desktop-linux . CONTRIBUTING.md lists every gate.

 Documentation

- Introduction : what it is and how it works

- Snapshots and refs

- Errors and recovery

- Skills

- CONCEPTS.md : vocabulary

- CONTRIBUTING.md , SECURITY.md , SUPPORT.md

representativeRepos.readmeText:
Auto Ontology

 Agents can retrieve documents and query databases, but reliability gates agentic analytics: a revenue metric answered faster is worth nothing if the number is wrong. Agents need a context layer that tells them where data lives, what it means, whether to use it, how to use it, where it came from, and what is similar. NVIDIA Auto Ontology is an open library that builds that layer from enterprise metadata, reconciles definitions across systems, and exposes it to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API. It complements the semantic models customers already own.

 It enables developers to:

- Discover: generate enterprise ontologies from metadata; connect existing ontologies and semantic models; build AI-ready knowledge graphs.

- Ground: give agents trusted business meaning for metrics, entities, and relationships; reconcile inconsistent definitions across systems.

- Validate: check generated queries against certified definitions and lineage; return provenance with every answer.

- Expose: serve context to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API.
Learn: fold certified corrections and usage back into the ontology, so shared context improves with every question.

 Benchmarks

 To run a text-to-SQL benchmark such as BIRD, refer to the
 ontology SQL evaluation repository .

 Licensing & contributions. Auto Ontology is distributed under the
 Apache License 2.0 . Third-party open-source components
bundled, linked, or otherwise used by this project are listed in
 THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md . This project
is currently not accepting external contributions.

 Key Features

- Natural-language querying of structured data — questions are translated to
SQL and executed against connected databases, powered by NVIDIA NIM.

- Semantic catalog / ontology layer over relational sources, stored in
Postgres alongside the catalog it describes.

- Authentication & RBAC —using Better Auth .

- Web UI for chat, analysis, data catalog, analytics, and settings.

- Flexible deployment — Helm chart for Kubernetes or Docker Compose for a
local stack.

 Software Components

 Component
 Technology
 Role
 Default port

 Frontend
 Next.js 16 (React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4), Better Auth, Prisma
 Web UI, authentication, API gateway
 3000

 Backend
 FastAPI (Python 3.12+), LangChain
 Chat / NL-to-SQL, catalog, datasource APIs
 3001

 Ingestion worker
 FastAPI (Python 3.12+)
 Ingests tabular data and writes embeddings
 3002

 Postgres + pgvector
 Relational Database
 App metadata, the catalog and ontology, vector store
 5432

 HashiCorp Vault
 Optional
 Secure storage of connection credentials
 —

 NVIDIA NIM

 Auto Ontology uses NVIDIA NIM endpoints for inference — either the hosted
 NVIDIA API catalog ( integrate.api.nvidia.com ) or
self-hosted NIMs. The defaults in .env.example are:

- LLM: nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b

- Embeddings: nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b

- Reranking: nvidia/llama-nemotron-rerank-vl-1b-v2

 The endpoints and models are configured via the DEFAULT_MODELS_ENDPOINT , DEFAULT_MODELS_MODEL ,
 EMBED_ENDPOINT , and EMBED_MODEL environment variables and require a
 DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY .

 Model triplets

 Each model role is configured by a triplet of environment variables —
 <PREFIX>_ENDPOINT (URL), <PREFIX>_API_KEY , and <PREFIX>_MODEL :

 Prefix
 Role

 DEFAULT_MODELS
 Shared default; every field below falls back to it.

 REASONING
 Main chat / NL-to-SQL model.

 NON_REASONING
 Lighter model used for entity extraction.

 EMBED
 Text-embedding model (must match between ingest and query).

 RERANK
 Reranker used by the retrieval flow.

 You can set a full triplet, only some of its fields, or none at all — any field
left unset falls back to the matching DEFAULT_MODELS_<FIELD> . So the simplest
setup is to fill in DEFAULT_MODELS_* and override per-triplet fields only where
they differ (e.g. EMBED_MODEL , NON_REASONING_MODEL ). *_API_KEY also falls
back to the legacy NVIDIA_API_KEY for backward compatibility.

 Quickstart

 This runs Auto-Ontology with Docker Compose against Wide World Importers,
Microsoft's sample sales database. You need Docker with Compose v2,
 uv , and an NVIDIA API key ( nvapi-... ) from
 build.nvidia.com .

-
 Clone the repository and create .env :

 git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology.git && cd auto-ontology
cp .env.example .env

 Then set these values in .env :

 DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY = nvapi-...
 AUTH_SECRET = <a long random string, e.g. from openssl rand -base64 32>
 APP_URL = http://localhost:3000
 POSTGRES_PASSWORD = <a new password>
 CONNECTION_STRINGS = postgresql://postgres:<the same password>@postgres:5432/wideworldimporters
 AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_PASSWORD = <a new password>
 PGADMIN_PASSWORD = <a new password>

 Compose publishes Postgres, pgAdmin, and the web app on the host, so replace
each default password before you start it. .env.example also sets an API
key per model role: replace each nvapi-your-api-key-here with your key, or
delete those lines so they fall back to DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY .

-
 Start Postgres and load the sample database. The seed script lives in
auto-ontology-eval; pass it the Postgres password you set:

 docker compose up -d --wait postgres
git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology-eval.git ../auto-ontology-eval
(cd ../auto-ontology-eval && uv sync && cp .env.example .env && \
 POSTGRES_PASSWORD= ' <the same password> ' \
 uv run python scripts/seed/seed_wwi.py --database-name wideworldimporters --drop)

-
 Build and start the rest of the stack:

 docker compose up -d --build

-
 Open http://localhost:3000 and sign in with AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_EMAIL and
 AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_PASSWORD from .env . Go to Settings → Semantic
Compilation and turn it on. Ingestion runs at startup; compilation starts
immediately and reports Semantic compilation is ready when it finishes.

-
 Ask a question in Chat :

 What was revenue for the USB food flash drive - sushi roll in Pennsylvania
in June 2015?

 The agent resolves revenue , product , and state to terms in the
ontology, follows their relationships to the joins it needs, and runs the
query. The answer comes back with its SQL and the steps that produced it,
so you can check the result against the source:

 Answer: Revenue for USB food flash drive - sushi roll in Pennsylvania in
 June 2015 was $588.80, from 3 invoice lines.

SQL: SELECT SUM(il.extendedprice) AS revenue, COUNT(*) AS invoice_lines
 FROM sales.invoicelines il
 JOIN sales.invoices i ON il.invoiceid = i.invoiceid
 JOIN warehouse.stockitems si ON il.stockitemid = si.stockitemid
 JOIN sales.customers c ON i.customerid = c.customerid
 JOIN application.cities ct ON c.deliverycityid = ct.cityid
 JOIN application.stateprovinces sp ON ct.stateprovinceid = sp.stateprovinceid
 WHERE si.stockitemname = 'USB food flash drive - sushi roll'
 AND sp.stateprovincename = 'Pennsylvania'
 AND i.invoicedate >= '2015-06-01' AND i.invoicedate < '2015-07-01'

Steps: Resolved terms: Invoice Line (revenue), Stock Item, State Province, Invoice
 Joined: invoice line -> invoice -> customer -> city -> state province
 Validated the filter values against the data, then executed

-
 Ask something the data can't answer. Wide World Importers has no
advertising data, so a question about ad spend has nothing to resolve
against. An agent connected through MCP checks answerability
first and asks you to clarify:

 You: What was return on ad spend for the sushi roll flash drive in June 2015?
Agent: check_answerable -> coverage 0.5; no term covers "ad spend"
Agent: I can find revenue for that product, but this data has no
 advertising spend, so I can't compute return on ad spend. Do you
 want June 2015 revenue instead, or is ad spend tracked in another
 source I should connect?

 If the UI loads without its left navigation after a restart, the browser is
holding a stale session cookie. Clear site data for localhost:3000 and sign in
again. For other setup failures, see the
 setup skill's troubleshooting guide .

 How it works

 Auto-Ontology works in three stages: it generates an ontology, people certify
it, and the agent answers questions from it.

 The ontology holds three kinds of definition:

- Terms. Business concepts such as Customer or Invoice Line , each with a
description and synonyms, mapped to the columns that hold them.

- SQL attributes. Reviewed SQL expressions under a term, such as a margin or
a rolling total. The agent reuses them, so answers compute each measure the
same way.

- Relationships. How tables join, including bridge tables, inferred from
keys and from the data.

 Generate. The ingestion service builds a first draft from the source
databases:

- Read sources: extract schemas, profile columns, and sample values into the
catalog.

- Name entities: extract terms table by table and map each to columns.

- Resolve relationships: infer joins between tables and bridge tables, and
suggest SQL attributes from query history.

- Write the ontology: store terms, relationships, and SQL attributes in
Postgres, with embeddings in pgvector for retrieval.

 The result is a semantic graph you can explore in the UI. In this example, one
compilation of Wide World Importers produced 31 terms; selecting Order shows
its description, related terms, mapped columns, and SQL attributes:

 Certify. People make the draft trustworthy:

- Test with real questions in Chat, or with check_answerable and
 ask_question over MCP.

- Refine terms, descriptions, and SQL attributes in the UI or through the API.

- Certify names, descriptions, and SQL attributes once they're correct.

 Answer. For each question, the agent:

- Classifies the intent and extracts the entities the question names.

- Retrieves candidate terms, columns, and SQL attributes by embedding search.

- Writes SQL from those candidates.

- Checks the filter values and the query against the database, repairing the
SQL when a check fails.

- Runs the query and returns the answer with its SQL and the steps it took.

 When the candidates can't support a query, the agent reports that the question
can't be answered from this data. Predictive questions go to KumoRFM when it's
configured (see Predictions ).

 In Chat, each answer shows its SQL, and you can view the rows, download them as
CSV, or read them as a chart:

 Auto-Ontology is compatible with Apache Ossie , the
open standard for exchanging semantic models. Ossie includes a
 converter for Auto-Ontology ,
which Auto-Ontology uses to import and export model definitions as Ossie YAML.
Use Settings → Import / Export , or POST /api/model/import and
 POST /api/model/export .

representativeRepos.readmeText:
Skills For Real Engineers

 My agent skills that I use every day to do real engineering - not vibe coding.

 Developing real applications is hard. Approaches like GSD, BMAD, and Spec-Kit try to help by owning the process. But while doing so, they take away your control and make bugs in the process hard to resolve.

 These skills are designed to be small, easy to adapt, and composable. They work with any model. They're based on decades of engineering experience. Hack around with them. Make them your own. Enjoy.

 If you want to keep up with changes to these skills, and any new ones I create, you can join ~60,000 other devs on my newsletter:

 Sign Up To The Newsletter

 Installation (30-second setup)

 A plugin updates itself. skills.sh copies editable files into your project, and you update them by hand. Pick one per agent, because installing both gives you every skill twice.

 1. Get the skills

 Claude Code
 claude plugin install mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official

 Updates itself by default.

 Codex
 codex plugin marketplace add mattpocock/skills
codex plugin add mattpocock-skills@mattpocock

 Updates itself at startup.

 GitHub Copilot (CLI and VS Code)
 copilot plugin marketplace add mattpocock/skills
copilot plugin install mattpocock-skills@mattpocock

 Then, once, add to ~/.copilot/settings.json :

 {
 "extraKnownMarketplaces" : {
 "mattpocock" : { "source" : { "source" : " github " , "repo" : " mattpocock/skills " }, "autoUpdate" : true }
 }
}

 In VS Code, run Chat: Install Plugin From Source and enter https://github.com/mattpocock/skills . It updates daily.

 Gemini CLI (manual updates)
 gemini skills install https://github.com/mattpocock/skills.git --path skills/engineering
gemini skills install https://github.com/mattpocock/skills.git --path skills/productivity

 Re-run both commands to update.

 Any other agent, or editable files (manual updates)
 npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills -a < agent > # cursor, opencode, devin, windsurf, amp, pi; omit -a to choose

 When the installer asks which skills to take, include setup-matt-pocock-skills . To update, run npx skills@latest update , and re-run add to pick up new skills.

 2. Run /setup-matt-pocock-skills

 In your agent, run it once per repo. It will:

- Ask you which issue tracker you want to use (GitHub, GitLab, local files, or anything else you describe)

- Ask you what labels you apply to tickets when you triage them ( /triage uses labels)

- Ask you where you want to save any docs we create

 3. Bam - you're ready to go.

 Why These Skills Exist

 I built these skills as a way to fix common failure modes I see with Claude Code, Codex, and other coding agents.

 #1: The Agent Didn't Do What I Want

 "No-one knows exactly what they want"

 David Thomas & Andrew Hunt, The Pragmatic Programmer

 The Problem . The most common failure mode in software development is misalignment. You think the dev knows what you want. Then you see what they've built - and you realize it didn't understand you at all.

 This is just the same in the AI age. There is a communication gap between you and the agent. The fix for this is a grilling session - getting the agent to ask you detailed questions about what you're building.

 The Fix is to use:

- /grill-me - for non-code uses

- /grill-with-docs - same as /grill-me , but adds more goodies (see below)

 These are my most popular skills. They help you align with the agent before you get started, and think deeply about the change you're making. Use them every time you want to make a change.

 #2: The Agent Is Way Too Verbose

 With a ubiquitous language, conversations among developers and expressions of the code are all derived from the same domain model.

 Eric Evans, Domain-Driven-Design

 The Problem : At the start of a project, devs and the people they're building the software for (the domain experts) are usually speaking different languages.

 I felt the same tension with my agents. Agents are usually dropped into a project and asked to figure out the jargon as they go. So they use 20 words where 1 will do.

 The Fix for this is a shared language. It's a document that helps agents decode the jargon used in the project.

Example

 Here's an example glossary (still named CONTEXT.md at that pinned commit, from before the skills renamed the convention), from my course-video-manager repo. Which one is easier to read?

- BEFORE : "There's a problem when a lesson inside a section of a course is made 'real' (i.e. given a spot in the file system)"

- AFTER : "There's a problem with the materialization cascade"

 This concision pays off session after session.

 This is built into /grill-with-docs . It's a grilling session, but that helps you build a shared language with the AI, and document hard-to-explain decisions in ADR's.

 It's hard to explain how powerful this is. It might be the single coolest technique in this repo. Try it, and see.

 Tip
 A shared language has many other benefits than reducing verbosity:

- Variables, functions and files are named consistently , using the shared language

- As a result, the codebase is easier to navigate for the agent

- The agent also spends fewer tokens on thinking , because it has access to a more concise language

 #3: The Code Doesn't Work

 "Always take small, deliberate steps. The rate of feedback is your speed limit. Never take on a task that’s too big."

 David Thomas & Andrew Hunt, The Pragmatic Programmer

 The Problem : Let's say that you and the agent are aligned on what to build. What happens when the agent still produces crap?

 It's time to look at your feedback loops. Without feedback on how the code it produces actually runs, the agent will be flying blind.

 The Fix : You need the usual tranche of feedback loops: static types, browser access, and automated tests.

 For automated tests, a red-green-refactor loop is critical. This is where the agent writes a failing test first, then fixes the test. This helps give the agent a consistent level of feedback that results in far better code.

 I've built a /tdd skill you can slot into any project. It encourages red-green-refactor and gives the agent plenty of guidance on what makes good and bad tests.

 For debugging, I've also built a /diagnosing-bugs skill that wraps best debugging practices into a disciplined loop, gated phase by phase.

 #4: We Built A Ball Of Mud

 "Invest in the design of the system every day ."

 Kent Beck, Extreme Programming Explained

 "The best modules are deep. They allow a lot of functionality to be accessed through a simple interface."

 John Ousterhout, A Philosophy Of Software Design

 The Problem : Most apps built with agents are complex and hard to change. Because agents can radically speed up coding, they also accelerate software entropy. Codebases get more complex at an unprecedented rate.

 The Fix for this is a radical new approach to AI-powered development: caring about the design of the code.

 This is built in to every layer of these skills:

- /to-spec quizzes you about which modules you're touching before creating a spec

 And crucially, /improve-codebase-architecture surveys a codebase for deepening opportunities and hands you the candidates. I recommend running it on your codebase once every few days. It is a survey, not a rescue: on a genuinely old codebase it will find real candidates, but it won't untangle the mud for you.

 Summary

 Software engineering fundamentals matter more than ever. These skills are my best effort at condensing these fundamentals into repeatable practices, to help you ship the best apps of your career. Enjoy.

 Reference

 These split on one axis: who can invoke them. User-invoked skills are reachable only when you type them (e.g. /grill-me ); their job is to orchestrate. Model-invoked skills can be invoked by you or reached for automatically by the agent when the task fits; they hold the reusable discipline. A user-invoked skill may invoke model-invoked skills, but never another user-invoked one.

 Engineering

 Skills I use daily for code work.

 User-invoked

- ask-matt : Ask which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the user-invoked skills in this repo.

- grill-with-docs : Grilling session that also builds your project's domain model, sharpening terminology and updating GLOSSARY.md and ADRs inline.

- triage : Move issues through a state machine of triage roles.

- improve-codebase-architecture : Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick.

- setup-matt-pocock-skills : Configure this repo for the engineering skills (issue tracker, triage labels, domain doc layout). Run once per repo before using the other engineering skills.

- to-spec : Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the issue tracker. No interview, just synthesizes what you've already discussed.

- to-tickets : Break any plan, spec, or conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, written as text in a local file, or as native blocking links on a real tracker.

- implement : Build the work described by a spec or set of tickets, driving /tdd at pre-agreed seams and closing out with /code-review before committing.

- implement-spec : Implement a whole spec on one integration branch. Works the tickets as a task graph, running implementer subagents across the ready frontier for maximum concurrency, then closes out with /code-review .

- wayfinder : Plan a huge chunk of work, more than one agent session can hold, as a shared map of decision tickets on the issue tracker, and resolve them one at a time until the way to the destination is clear.

- retro : Suggest improvements to the coding agent's environment (navigation, automated checks, coding standards, steering files, tooling) after a session, most severe first.

 Model-invoked

- prototype : Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question, either a single shareable HTML file for state/logic questions, or several radically different UI variations toggleable from one route.

- diagnosing-bugs : Disciplined diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions: build a feedback loop that goes red on this bug → minimise → hypothesise → instrument → fix → regression-test.

- research : Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a cited Markdown file in the repo, run as a background agent.

- tdd : Test-driven development with a red-green-refactor loop. Builds features or fixes bugs one vertical slice at a time.

- domain-modeling : Actively build and sharpen a project's domain model: challenge terms against the glossary, stress-test with edge-case scenarios, and update GLOSSARY.md and ADRs inline.

- codebase-design : Shared discipline and vocabulary for designing deep modules: a lot of behaviour behind a small interface, placed at a clean seam, testable through that interface.

- code-review : Two-axis review of the diff since a fixed point: Standards (does it follow the repo's coding standards, plus a Fowler smell baseline?) and Spec (does it faithfully implement the originating issue/spec?), run as parallel sub-agents so neither pollutes the other.

- pr : The shape a pull request body should take: a summary as the smallest visual that makes the change clear, before/after evidence that it works, and a merge-danger call (one-way or two-way door, plus blast radius).

- wizard : Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform: provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover.

 Productivity

 General workflow tools, not code-specific.

 User-invoked

- grill-me : Get relentlessly interviewed about a plan or design until every branch of the design tree is resolved.

- handoff : Compact the current conversation into a handoff document so...

items.overview: 社区正在把智能体从聊天式能力模块，推向具备执行闭环、工具调用、记忆和多阶段编排的工业化系统。
items.what: 多个高增项目的共同演进方向，是让 Agent 从单轮交互接口升级为可持续运行、可调度、可接入外部工具链的全链路系统。
items.why: 其背后的范式转移是，单轮问答式 Agent 已无法覆盖真实业务中的长链路任务，行业开始追求具备稳定执行、自主性和可复用流水线的智能体基础能力。
items.how: 支撑这一趋势的通用方法论包括多 Agent 协同架构、工具调用协议、任务编排器、长期记忆层以及浏览器/终端等执行接口的标准化接入。
items.risk: 潜在风险在于，Agent 工业化很容易堆叠复杂度；如果缺少评测、权限控制和故障回滚机制，系统会在真实环境中暴露稳定性与安全性问题。

representativeRepos.readmeText:
Auto Ontology

 Agents can retrieve documents and query databases, but reliability gates agentic analytics: a revenue metric answered faster is worth nothing if the number is wrong. Agents need a context layer that tells them where data lives, what it means, whether to use it, how to use it, where it came from, and what is similar. NVIDIA Auto Ontology is an open library that builds that layer from enterprise metadata, reconciles definitions across systems, and exposes it to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API. It complements the semantic models customers already own.

 It enables developers to:

- Discover: generate enterprise ontologies from metadata; connect existing ontologies and semantic models; build AI-ready knowledge graphs.

- Ground: give agents trusted business meaning for metrics, entities, and relationships; reconcile inconsistent definitions across systems.

- Validate: check generated queries against certified definitions and lineage; return provenance with every answer.

- Expose: serve context to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API.
Learn: fold certified corrections and usage back into the ontology, so shared context improves with every question.

 Benchmarks

 To run a text-to-SQL benchmark such as BIRD, refer to the
 ontology SQL evaluation repository .

 Licensing & contributions. Auto Ontology is distributed under the
 Apache License 2.0 . Third-party open-source components
bundled, linked, or otherwise used by this project are listed in
 THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md . This project
is currently not accepting external contributions.

 Key Features

- Natural-language querying of structured data — questions are translated to
SQL and executed against connected databases, powered by NVIDIA NIM.

- Semantic catalog / ontology layer over relational sources, stored in
Postgres alongside the catalog it describes.

- Authentication & RBAC —using Better Auth .

- Web UI for chat, analysis, data catalog, analytics, and settings.

- Flexible deployment — Helm chart for Kubernetes or Docker Compose for a
local stack.

 Software Components

 Component
 Technology
 Role

 Frontend
 Next.js 16 (React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4), Better Auth, Prisma
 Web UI, authentication, API gateway

 Backend

 Chat / NL-to-SQL, catalog, datasource APIs

 Ingestion worker
 FastAPI (Python 3.12+)
 Ingests tabular data and writes embeddings

 Postgres + pgvector
 Relational Database
 App metadata, the catalog and ontology, vector store
